source_policy: Reference concepts only; no original schema or patient-record reuse claimed

poe: provider-order categories and transaction concepts; no direct field mapping
pharmacy: separate medication pharmacy records; authored schema and dispensing milestone
prescriptions: prescription identity and stop-time meaning; medication_order is an authored representation

adaptations: All records, SQL types and constraints are authored
patients/admissions retain MIMIC-inspired patient/stay grains; optional profile/detail split-storage tables are authored
No generic object, object_type or clinical_order tables are present
Laboratory, medication and procedure orders are distinct business identities with independent local ID namespaces
Identity group answers are private evaluation annotations, not input DB tables
Separate order tables intentionally replace the MIMIC poe organization; medication_order represents a prescription, not pharmacy dispensing.
pharmacy is a simplified authored dispensing object with dispensed_at, not a replica of MIMIC pharmacy columns. emar references pharmacy directly.
lab_order is authored. Its required subject_id preserves outpatient attribution when hadm_id is NULL; no direct replication of MIMIC specimen structure is claimed.
procedure_episode uses familiar start/end timing but is hospital-level authored storage; original ICU procedureevents/stay_id is not reproduced.
Synthetic subject IDs use 1xxxxxxx, admission IDs 2xxxxxxx; shuffled independent order IDs use 3xxxxxxx, with deliberate partial inter-order namespace overlap.
Prescription/dispensing/administration joins follow authored declared keys, not original MIMIC join identities.
labevents.charttime is specimen collection time; the authored clean pathway enforces collection before receipt, result availability and verification. Measurement execution time is not recorded.
Constant summary_status removed. The signed-summary table excludes drafts and records post-discharge signing.
